findings.issue: Caret ranges on the ~4-month-old Astro 7 major (^7.4.2, @astrojs/node ^11.1.9) mean minor-release churn will flow in automatically; this is normal practice but the APIs used predate v7, so an earlier major would behave identically.
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is; optionally pin exact versions in CI to make the recently-stable major fully reproducible.

summary: The app runs on the current stable Astro 7.4.x but is maximally conservative: only APIs stable since Astro 2-4 (output: 'server', node adapter, Astro.params/url/response, class: directive, processed scripts) appear, with zero experimental flags or unstable names. No Astro 7 headline features (Advanced Routing, route caching, CDN cache providers) or newer stable features (Actions, server islands, View Transitions) are used — interactivity is plain DOM. Risk of experimental-API breakage is essentially nil.
